title: Physiological markers of low-altitude exercise load for predicting acute mountain sickness: development of an interpretable machine learning model and research web calculator.
summary: A locked equal-weight logistic-regression, random-forest and SVM ensemble used five predictors to estimate questionnaire-defined acute mountain sickness after rapid ascent. Development and an independent external cohort provide a bounded prediction result; the research calculator does not establish prospective utility.
ai_technology: Equal-weight logistic regression, random forest and SVM ensemble

evidence.tested: The development cohort included 111 participants, 51 meeting questionnaire-defined AMS criteria; an independent external cohort was evaluated. Exercise-related physiological associations were also reported.
evidence.unknown: Outcome is questionnaire-defined AMS; external cohort testing and a web calculator do not establish prospective clinical or field utility.
evidence.ai_role: Equal-weight logistic regression, random forest and SVM ensemble

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
